chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
About a woman for whom dawn rises while she is menstruating in the month of Ramadan.

Then when morning comes she becomes pure, though she had already eaten, and then she prays al-ẓuhr and al-ʿaṣr. What should she do regarding that day in which she became pure? He said: “She refrains in fasting, but it is not counted for her.”

key_terms.تَصُومُ: she observes fasting for the remainder of the day
key_terms.حَائِضٌ: a woman in the state of menstruation
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the time of the obligatory fast
key_terms.صَلَّتِ الظُّهْرَ وَالْعَصْرَ: she performed the noon and afternoon prayers after becoming pure
key_terms.وَلَا تَعْتَدُّ بِهِ: it is not counted as a valid fast for legal fulfillment

ai.seo_question: If a woman becomes pure from menstruation after dawn in Ramadan, does that day count as a fast?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a menstruating woman who becomes pure during the daytime in Ramadan after having already eaten. She is instructed to observe the rest of the day as a fast, but that day does not count as a valid obligatory fast and must therefore not be reckoned as fulfilled.
